summary: Edwin F. Bryant is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at Columbia University (~1991–1997). He taught at Harvard University (~1998–2002) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University (~2003).

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson (1840–1890) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology after studying at Trinity College Dublin (~1858–1861). He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (~1888–1890).

Edwin Gerow (1931–2018) worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Professor of Religion and Humanities at Reed College (~1985–1997) and was Editor-in-Chief of the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1993–1998).

Edwin Norris (1795–1872) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He was a clerk at the East India Company (1818–1837), translator at the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and held several secretarial and librarian posts at the Royal Asiatic Society.

Edwin Whitfield Fay (1865–1920) was a linguist and Indologist. Educated at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig, he held posts at the University of Michigan, Washington and Lee University, and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda (1926–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen, Meijo, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Eido Tai Shimano (1932–2018) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Ryutaku-ji and the University of Hawaiʻi. He was abbot of the Zen Studies Society (~1965–2010) and led New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Imoto (1930–2014) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1949–1953) and held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (~1964–1996) and Momoyama Gakuin University (~1996–2001).

Eiichi Makino (1878–1970) worked in philosophy and other fields after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1903). He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1938), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College (~1957–1966), Kyushu, Chuo, and Tohoku Universities.

Eiichi Yamaguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who was a graduate student at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and subsequently served there as a Research Assistant (attested 1991).

Eiki Hoshino (1943–) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After studying at Taisho University (~1963–1967), he served as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director there (~1980–2013).

Eisaku Okada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014) and later served as a part-time lecturer there (attested 2015). In 2014, he was also affiliated with JSPS and Koyasan University.
Eisei Kojima is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1976) and as president of Doho University (attested 1976).

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1934–1937) under Gyoo Kageyama. He later held posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (~1949–1984).
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
Eiyin Yasuda (1938–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Gyōin Hashimoto (~1950–1978) and completed studies at Ryukoku University (~1957–1961).
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Sōkatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Toyo University and Sera Monastery, among other institutions. He held posts at Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1891), Toyo University (1916), and Toyo Bunko (1940).
Eki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and held a DC2 research fellowship at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (both attested 2020).

Ekyo Ejima (1939–1999) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at the University of Tokyo and studied at Göttingen. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and board chairman of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.
